https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/a.text: Tarun Tejpal’s acquittal in 2021 was challenged by the Goa government. Photograph: Frédéric Soltan/Corbis/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Tarun Tejpal’s acquittal in 2021 was challenged by the Goa government. Photograph: Frédéric Soltan/Corbis/Getty Images India High-profile Indian journalist jailed for 10 years for raping colleague Tarun Tejpal, ex-editor of Tehelka magazine, was initially acquitted in 2021 in case that drew nationwide attention Agence France-Press in Mumbai Thu 6 Aug 2026 07.47 EDT First published on Thu 6 Aug 2026 04.05 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google An Indian court has sentenced a high-profile former editor of an investigative news magazine to 10 years in prison after convicting him of raping a junior colleague, overturning his acquittal in a case that drew nationwide attention. Tarun Tejpal, 63, the founder and former editor of Tehelka magazine, was accused of raping a journalist in the lift of a five-star hotel in the western coastal state of Goa during an event in November 2013. He was arrested and spent seven months in jail until the supreme court granted him bail. A court in Goa acquitted Tejpal of charges including rape, sexual harassment and wrongful restraint in 2021. The government of Goa challenged the acquittal before the Bombay high court, which set aside the trial court’s verdict and sentenced him to 10 years in jail on Thursday. “He has been convicted to 10 years of rigorous imprisonment. He has been given two weeks’ time to surrender,” the police investigator Sunita Sawant, who led the case against Tejpal, told reporters. The court also ordered him to pay a £3,900 fine, he said. Tejpal, 63, said he would challenge the conviction in the supreme court. He had initially blamed the assault on “a lapse of judgement” but later alleged the case against him was part of a vendetta by the Bharatiya Janata party (BJP) government in Goa. “For the past 13 years, they have been pursuing me as a part of a political vendetta,” he said after conviction. Sawant told reporters: “This is a sentence where a girl has stood up for her rights … so this judgment is very important for women who are working in any sector.” The case emerged at a time when India’s handling of sexual assault cases was under intense scrutiny after the gang-rape and murder of a 23-year-old student on a Delhi bus in December 2012. That attack triggered nationwide protests and international outrage, and prompted the government to strengthen the country’s rape laws. Tejpal’s case severely damaged the authority and credibility of Tehelka, which had historically championed women’s rights and social justice. The magazine continues to operate under new leadership, but it has failed to regain the influence it had before the 2013 case. Beállítom "Az itt keletkező vizek tekintetében mi a legkevésbé sem vagyunk víznagyhatalom, sőt az egyik legszegényebb ország vagyunk. Az országon tulajdonképpen három ponton folyik be, és számtalan ponton folyik ki a víz” – mondta V. Németh Zsolt, a Fidesz országgyűlési képviselője, az előző kormány vízgazdálkodásért felelős államtitkára a 24.hu-nak . Ez ellentmond Orbán Viktor korábbi kijelentésének, a volt miniszterelnök a vízzabáló akkumulátorgyárak Magyarországra telepítésének védelmében ugyanis 2023-ban azt mondta a parlamentben, hogy Magyarországot nem sújtja vízhiány, így semmi problémát nem jelent a gyárak működése. „Magyarországról több víz távozik, mint amennyi bejön. Ez azt jelenti, hogy nekünk van feleslegünk. Azt föl tudjuk fogni. Ha akarjuk, és szükség van rá, azt a vízmennyiséget a magyar csatornarendszeren keresztül bárhova el tudjuk vinni. Ha szükség van rá. Magyarország ma semmilyen vízhiányban nem szenved, és ha az igény nő, akkor képesek vagyunk ezt az igényt kielégíteni” – mondta. A volt miniszterelnök szavai az elmúlt hetekben Lázár János korábbi építési és közlekedési miniszter tavaly decemberben tett kijelentésével együtt kerültek vissza a köztudatba. Lázár tavaly decemberben, még miniszterként, a bizottsági meghallgatásán nyilvánosan elismerte , hogy „a kormány hibát követett el, amikor nem épített nagy víztározókat tíz évvel ezelőtt”, és csak olyan árvízvédelmi tározók épültek, amelyek nem alkalmasak a vízvisszatartásra. Lázár arról beszélt, “őrültség, hogy kiengedjük az édesvizet, „olyan földrajzi, olyan természeti jelenségek vannak, amelyek brutális aggodalomra adnak okot”. A Fidesz a hetek óta tartó hőhullám, a Duna alacsony vízállása és az energiaválság miatt kapkodással, felkészületlenséggel és alkalmatlansággal vádolta a Tisza-kormányt, Bóka János, a Fidesz frakcióvezetője például arról beszélt, „hosszú hetek óta lehet tudni”, hogy alakul a Duna vízállása, és hogy „a jelenlegi helyzet bekövetkezik”, mégsem készült fel rá a kormány. Bóka szerint az elmúlt 16 év eredménye, hogy egyáltalán még működik a villamosenergia-hálózat, és Orbán Viktor a vízmegtartás és az energiabiztonság szempontjából is jobb állapotban adta át az országot, mint ahogy átvette 2010-ben. A Fidesz kommunikációs stratégiájának hitelességét a téma szakértőinek és kutatóinak megszólalásain kívül Lázár János korábbi – Orbán Viktoréval ellentétes – kijelentései is cáfolták, erről ebben a cikkben írtunk részletesen . A 24.hu a témában megkereste V. Németh Zsoltot is, ez Energiaügyi Minisztérium korábbi, vízgazdálkodásért felelős államtitkárát. V. Németh azzal kapcsolatban, hogy lehetett volna többet tenni a vízmegtartásért, azt mondta: “Mindig lehet többet tenni, de ehhez 300 milliárdos helyett ezermilliárdos nagyságrendű forrásról kéne beszélnünk.” A korábbi államtitkár szerint vízügyekre 330-340 milliárd forint körüli összeg állt rendelkezésükre, amelyből nagyjából 280 milliárd a víz visszatartására, a vízkészletek növelésére ment el. V. Németh arról is beszélt, Magyarországon az elmúlt évben annyi eső esett, “mint Izraelben, Botswanában, és alig több, mint Marokkóban”, és itt keletkező vizek tekintetében “az egyik legszegényebb ország vagyunk”. V. Németh szerint komoly problémát jelent, hogy ahol természetesen megjelenhetne a víz, most városok és magánföldek vannak. A gazdák az előző kormány Vizet a Tájba! programjában ugyan felajánlhatták az elárasztható területeiket, de "ha úgy szeretnénk víztározókat létesíteni, mint eddig, és fizetünk annak, akinek a földjét elárasztjuk, ahhoz a világ pénze nem elég.” V. Németh a lapnak több szükséges intézkedést is felsorolt, amelyek az elmúlt években nem, vagy csak részben valósultak meg, és üdvözölte, hogy az új kormányban a vízgazdálkodás ügye egységesebb lett a Gajdos László vezette Élő Környezetért Felelős Minisztériumban. A lap megkereste Nagy István korábbi agrárminisztert, aki azonban csak az előző kormány eredményeinek felsorolásával felelt a kérdéseikre, és az Áder János által alapított, rengeteg közpénzzel támogatott Kék Bolygó Alapítványt is, amely az általuk támogatott klímakonferenciákról és természetvédelmi filmfesztiválokról írt. https://www.mfa.gov.lv/en/article/parlia.text: Parliamentary Secretary Dace Melbārde to participate in the EU General Affairs Council Published: 12.10.2026. Photo: Laura Celmiņa, Ministry of Foreign Affairs Facebook X / Twitter Linkedin Threads On 13 October 2026, a meeting of the EU General Affairs Council will take place in Luxembourg, where Latvia will be represented by Parliamentary Secretary Dace Melbārde. The meeting is planned to include an exchange of views on the draft conclusions of the European Council meeting on 15–16 October, covering issues such as Russia’s war against Ukraine, the situation in the Middle East, EU security and enlargement, security and defence, migration and competitiveness. There will also be a discussion on the EU Multiannual Financial Framework for 2028–2034, focusing on the updated negotiating framework document, known as the NegoBox, prepared by the Irish Presidency of the Council of the EU. The Irish Presidency will provide an update on the latest developments and next steps in the process of simplifying EU legislation, as well as on the current situation in Hungary regarding respect for EU values. It is also planned to approve the Council’s conclusions on inclusive democratic participation and societal resilience. An informal lunch discussion on the review of the EU’s pre-enlargement policy is also scheduled. The General Affairs Council examines matters concerning more than one EU policy, such as negotiations on EU enlargement, preparations for the European Council, the EU’s Multiannual Financial Framework, as well as the rule of law, institutional and administrative matters. https://www.naharnet.com/stories/en/3235.text: European air traffic targeted by several new threats after week of hoaxes Officials across Europe reported more bomb threats against multiple flights on Friday, following a string of hoaxes that have caused flight diversions this week. No suspicious items were found and no one was injured, but the threats have raised concern because they came as Europe digests a slew of other recent disruptions — including attacks on supermarket refrigeration systems and drone incursions. French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu's office said Friday that "four new bomb threats were made today against aircraft flying over French territory." The planes landed safely and bomb disposal experts were conducting inspections. The statement didn't give further details on the flights affected. A flight from Prague to Bucharest operated by Romanian carrier Tarom received a bomb threat, but it landed at its intended destination. Airport administration officials said the threat proved to be false. Portuguese police said they were informed of a bomb threat targeting a Ryanair flight traveling from Lisbon to Rome, and carried out a security inspection once the aircraft landed in Lisbon. Passengers and luggage scheduled to travel to Rome underwent additional security screening before boarding. Police in Venice said a WizzAir flight from Prague to Rome was diverted to the Italian city after a bomb alert. Passengers were evacuated after the aircraft landed, and authorities were carrying out security checks. The inspections had so far produced negative results, according to police. Air traffic at the airport was temporarily suspended but resumed. Meanwhile, police in Denmark and the Czech Republic both said they investigated threats to air traffic. In the Danish capital, Copenhagen, police said Friday they went to the airport for a second consecutive day "in connection with threats directed at air traffic" as a precautionary measure. They said they assessed that there had been no danger to passengers or to others at the airport, and that air traffic was proceeding safely and without disruption. Czech police also said they were again dealing with threats against planes on Friday. They said necessary security measures were taken in cooperation with Prague's Vaclav Havel Airport that had "a minimal impact on the normal operations at the airport." Airport spokesperson Denisa Hejtmánková said a total of nine flights were threatened — arriving flights from Denmark, Spain and Britain, and departing flights to the Netherlands, Cyprus, Romania, Italy and Britain. No clear evidence on who is behind the threats More than two dozen flights were affected by threats earlier in the week, with some diverted as authorities scrambled to rule out any danger. Fake bomb threats are relatively common but it is unusual to see so many in such a short period. It remains unclear who is behind the wave of airline hoaxes, which come at a time of increased geopolitical tensions and warnings from authorities that Russia may be ramping up so-called hybrid threats in Europe. Authorities have not attributed the threats to any group or state actor, and no evidence has emerged linking the hoaxes to a government. An email containing the threat sent Thursday to airport authorities in Rome and reviewed by The Associated Press purported to come from a group describing itself as anti-feminist and claiming it was targeting a "feminist regime." Another European airport received a threat with similar wording, but it was unclear if it came from the same sender. Bomb threats are on pilots' minds and create unnecessary tension, but crews are prepared to respond professionally, said Paul Reuter, vice president of the European Cockpit Association. Pilots review procedures with cabin crews, identify airports where they could divert and may carry extra fuel, he said. Reuter called the use of civil aviation for geopolitical disruption or hoaxes "totally unacceptable." Irish state broadcaster also received a threat In Ireland, the Dublin headquarters of national broadcaster RTE was evacuated Friday after a bomb threat, and live broadcasts were replaced with pre-recorded programs. Ireland's police force, An Garda Síochána, said it was "aware of a threat made against media organisations here and in Europe." It said that it has been liaising with Irish media organizations and the threat will be investigated. Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin said the threats to RTE and others "just illustrates how relatively simple it can be to cause disruption and to undermine the normal operation of society through unconventional activities of this kind, which are designed to cause fear and anxiety."
